11. State the principle of Homogeneity. Test the validity of equation p=mv², where p, m and v stand for linear momentum,
mass and velocity respectively.
Ans:- The principle of homogeneity states that all terms in a physically meaningful equation must have the same dimensions.
This principle is used to check the correctness of equations in terms of their dimensional consistency.
Testing the Validity of the Equation: p=mv²
Here, p = linear momentum m = mass v = velocity
Dimensional Formulae
Momentum(p)=mv Dimensional formula of momentum p: [M] [L] [𝑇−1]
Dimensional formula of mass m: [M] Dimensional formula of velocity v: [L] [𝑇−1] Thus Dimensional formula of v²: [𝐿2] [𝑇−2]
Now Check the dimensions of each side
The given equation is p=mv² Left-hand side(LHS): Dimensional formula of momentum p: [M] [L] [𝑇−1]
Right-hand side(RHS): Dimensional formula of mv²:[M]. [𝐿2] [𝑇−2] = [M][𝐿2][𝑇−2]
Here RHS and LHS are doesn’t match so given equation is dimensionally incorrect.

15. Why are the offspring produced from cross-breeding sterile?
Ans:- The offspring produced from cross-breeding are often sterile due to differences in the number of chromosomes between
the parent species. When two species with different chromosome numbers cross-breed, their offspring may inherit an
unbalanced set of chromosomes, which prevents proper pairing and segregation during reproduction. This leads to sterility,
as seen in hybrids like mules (the offspring of a horse and a donkey), which are sterile because horses and donkeys have
different chromosome numbers.
16. In order to protect and promote the medicinal herbs found in Nepal, it is essential to train the local people on the
processing of herbs and their use. Explain your opinions.
Ans:- Training local people in Nepal on the processing and use of medicinal herbs is crucial for preserving traditional
knowledge and ensuring sustainable harvesting practices. Educating them about proper techniques can enhance the quality
of the herbs and create opportunities for value-added products. Additionally, such training can boost local economies by
promoting the herbal industry while safeguarding biodiversity. This approach helps balance conservation efforts with
economic development, benefiting both the environment and local communities.
